unit.title: Preparing for the Oral History Interview

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned what makes a question good. Today: build a real, organized set of questions for your own interview.

A strong oral-history interview usually moves through life in order: ਬਚਪਨ (childhood), ਜਵਾਨੀ (youth), and adulthood, with a few open questions for each period. This structure helps the person you're interviewing follow a natural timeline, and helps you organize the ਕਹਾਣੀਆਂ (stories) you gather. Write at least two genuine open-ended questions for each of the three life periods — six questions total — about your own ਪਰਿਵਾਰ (family) elder's real life. Keep every question open-ended, using yesterday's ਕਿਹੋ ਜਿਹਾ/ਕਿਵੇਂ/ਕਿਉਂ pattern.
You now have a real, organized question list ready for an actual interview. Tomorrow we'll practice the listening skills that make an interview genuinely go well, not just the questions themselves.

objectives: Organize interview questions by life period: childhood, youth, adulthood
Write six genuine open-ended questions for a real family elder
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's open-question skill.
2. Introduce the three-life-period structure.
3. Have the child write two questions per period about their own family elder.
4. Check each question against the open-ended pattern.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: active listening.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide one example question per life period as a model before the child writes their own
Ready for more: ask them to identify which of their six questions they expect will produce the richest, most detailed answer, and why
Every Gurmukhi word used in this lesson was checked against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: A complete answer is six genuine open-ended questions (two per life period: childhood, youth, adulthood) about the student's own family elder — content varies by student, evaluated against the open-ended and life-period-organization criteria.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'oral-history capstone' description, producing the actual question list the student will use for their real interview.

generationData.instructions: Write two open-ended questions for each life period.
